{{for|the code-breaking method| Turingery}}

In [[mathematics]], '''Turing's method''' is used to verify that for any given [[Gram point]] {{math|''g''<sub>''m''</sub>}} there lie ''m''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 zeros of {{math|''ζ''(''s'')}}, in the region {{math|0 < Im(''s'') < Im(''g''<sub>''m''</sub>)}}, where {{math|''ζ''(''s'')}} is the [[Riemann zeta function]].<ref>{{cite book| last=Edwards | first=H. M. | authorlink=Harold Edwards (mathematician) | title=Riemann's zeta function | series=Pure and Applied Mathematics | volume=58 | location=New York-London |publisher=[[Academic Press]] | year=1974 | isbn=0-12-232750-0 | zbl=0315.10035}}</ref> It was discovered by [[Alan Turing]] and published in 1953,<ref>{{cite journal| last1=Turing| first1=A. M. | author1-link=Alan Turing | title=Some Calculations of the Riemann Zeta-Function | doi=10.1112/plms/s3-3.1.99 | year=1953| journal=[[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]] | volume=s3-3| issue=1| pages=99–117 }}</ref> although that proof contained errors and a correction was published in 1970 by R. Sherman Lehman.<ref>{{cite journal| last1=Lehman| first1=R. S. | title=On the Distribution of Zeros of the Riemann Zeta-Function | doi=10.1112/plms/s3-20.2.303| year=1970| journal=Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society | volume=s3-20| issue=2 | pages=303–320 }}</ref>

For every integer ''i'' with {{math| ''i'' < ''n''}} we find a list of Gram points <math> \{g_i \mid 0\leqslant i \leqslant m \} </math> and a complementary list <math> \{h_i \mid 0\leqslant i \leqslant m \} </math>, where {{math|''g''<sub>''i''</sub> }} is the smallest number such that 

:<math> (-1)^i Z(g_i + h_i) > 0, </math>

where ''Z''(''t'') is the Hardy [[Z function]]. Note that {{math| g<sub>i</sub> }} may be negative or zero. Assuming that <math> h_m = 0 </math> and there exists some integer ''k'' such that <math> h_k = 0 </math>, then if

:<math> 1 + \frac{1.91 + 0.114\log(g_{m+k}/2\pi) + \sum_{j=m+1}^{m+k-1}h_j}{g_{m+k} - g_m} < 2, </math>

and

:<math> -1 - \frac{1.91 + 0.114\log(g_m/2\pi) + \sum_{j=1}^{k-1}h_{m-j}}{g_m - g_{m-k}} > -2,  </math>

Then the bound is achieved and we have that there are exactly ''m''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 zeros of {{math|''ζ''(''s'')}}, in the region {{math|0 < Im(''s'') < Im(''g''<sub>''m''</sub>)}}.
